title: Deaf Lantern
text:
The absent ones blow and the night is dense. The night has the color of the dead man's eyelids.


All night I make the night. All night I write. Word by word I write the night.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Pizarnik's incantatory repetition of night as both action and substance.

title: Forms
text:
I do not know whether bird or cage

murderous hand

or dead young woman panting in the great dark throat

or silent

but perhaps oral as a fountain

perhaps minstrel

or princess in the highest tower.
editorial_note: Oral is kept rather than softened, preserving the poem's strange bodily register.

title: Twilight
text:
The shadow covers watched petals

The wind carries off the last gesture of a leaf

The alien and doubly mute sea

in the summer made merciful by its lights


A desire from here

A memory from there
editorial_note: The translation keeps the spare demonstratives of distance: here and there.

title: Beggar Voice
text:
And still I dare to love

the sound of light in a dead hour,

the color of time on an abandoned wall.


In my gaze I have lost everything.

It is so far to ask. So near to know there is nothing.
editorial_note: The final sentence preserves the original's stark opposition between asking and knowing absence.

title: Harp of Silence...
text:
Harp of silence

where fear nests.

Lunar moan of things

signifying absence.


Space of closed color.

Someone knocks and assembles

a coffin for the hour,

another coffin for the light.
editorial_note: Closed color and lunar moan keep the poem's compressed surreal images.

title: Like Wingless Wind Locked in My Eyes...
text:
Like wingless wind locked in my eyes

is the call of death.

Only an angel will bind me to the sun.

Where the angel,

where his word.


Oh to pierce with wine the gentle necessity of being.
editorial_note: The title follows the first line and keeps the poem's abrupt invocation intact.

title: Recognition
text:
You make the silence of the lilacs fluttering

in my tragedy of wind in the heart.

You made my life into a children's tale

where shipwrecks and deaths

are pretexts for adorable ceremonies.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the dark tenderness of ceremonies that aestheticize disaster.

title: Ambushed in My Writing...
text:
Ambushed in my writing

you sing in my poem.

Hostage of your sweet voice

petrified in my memory.

Bird clinging to its flight.

Air tattooed by an absent one.

Clock that beats with me

so that I never wake.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the paradoxes of capture and flight that structure the poem.
